news.title: Blockchain.com Pursues CFTC Approval to Launch US Crypto Derivatives and Prediction Markets
news.body: Blockchain.com has applied for DCM and FCM licenses to offer crypto derivatives and prediction markets in the US. If approved, Blockchain.com would directly challenge established US exchanges, giving US institutional and retail traders new regulated options for crypto-based financial products. Competing exchanges such as CME and CBOE may need to accelerate product innovation and licensing strategies to maintain market share.

news.title: DailyPay Securitises $200M in On-Demand Pay Receivables to Fund Expansion
news.body: DailyPay completed a $200 million asset-backed securitisation of its On-Demand Pay receivables, unlocking new capital for growth. This financing enables DailyPay to expand its payroll solutions to more US employers, who are increasingly seeking flexible wage access to attract and retain workers in a competitive labor market. Traditional payroll providers like ADP and Paychex face mounting pressure to offer similar real-time pay features.

news.title: Thailand SEC Sets October 16 Launch for Bitcoin and Ether ETF Rules
news.body: Thailand's SEC will implement new rules for bitcoin and ether ETFs on October 16, establishing requirements for custody and trading safeguards. The scheduled rollout aims to position Thailand as a regional hub for regulated crypto investment products, drawing interest from global ETF issuers and institutional investors. Other Asian markets, such as Singapore and Hong Kong, may respond by advancing their own crypto ETF frameworks.

news.title: Singapore Central Bank Mandates Independent AI Reviews for Banks
news.body: Singapore’s central bank now requires banks to conduct independent reviews of AI projects before deployment. Banks operating in Singapore must allocate resources for third-party audits and compliance, which could increase project costs but aims to prevent operational failures and reputational damage from unchecked AI use. International banks with Singapore branches, such as HSBC and Citi, must update their AI governance processes to meet the new standard.

news.title: Standard Chartered Expands Digital Asset Custody Services to Singapore
news.body: Standard Chartered has launched digital asset custody services in Singapore, expanding its crypto infrastructure for institutional clients in Asia. This launch challenges local custodians and signals rising demand from asset managers and funds seeking secure crypto storage. Global banks such as HSBC and DBS may accelerate their digital asset custody offerings in Singapore to compete for institutional crypto mandates.

perspective: Blockchain.com’s CFTC application and Standard Chartered’s Singapore custody launch signal regulatory and institutional shifts in US and Asian crypto markets.
